ingredients.name: Water (Aqua)
ingredients.function: Main liquid base that dissolves other ingredients.
ingredients.why: Water itself has no ingredient-specific concern at normal use. The quality and preservation of the finished product matter more than the water.
ingredients.health: No ingredient-specific concern.
ingredients.dependsOn: Not applicable.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.function: Humectant: holds moisture in skin and products. In food it is a sweetener and moisture keeper.
ingredients.why: Long history of use. Safety panels such as the Cosmetic Ingredient Review have found it safe as used in cosmetics, and food-safety committees have not set a numerical limit for it in food.
ingredients.health: No notable systemic concern at normal use levels.
ingredients.irritation: Rarely irritating. Pure glycerin on broken skin may sting.
ingredients.dependsOn: Very large amounts swallowed can cause stomach upset.
ingredients.precautions: None specific for normal use.

ingredients.name: Sodium Laureth Sulfate
ingredients.function: Foaming cleansing agent (surfactant) in shampoos, body washes and cleaners.
ingredients.why: Documented skin, scalp and eye irritation, especially with long contact or high concentration. It is milder than sodium lauryl sulfate, so most people tolerate it in rinse-off products.
ingredients.health: The main documented concern is irritation, not whole-body toxicity, at normal rinse-off use. Ethoxylated ingredients can contain traces of 1,4-dioxane, a manufacturing by-product that producers are expected to keep low.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate skin, scalp and eyes, particularly if left on or used often.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and how long it stays on the skin.
ingredients.precautions: Rinse well. Avoid eye contact. Stop use if the scalp becomes red or itchy.
groups: People with eczema or very sensitive skin or scalp

ingredients.name: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
ingredients.function: Strong foaming cleansing agent (surfactant).
ingredients.why: It is used as a reference irritant in dermatology skin tests, which shows it irritates skin more readily than most cleansers.
ingredients.health: Irritation is the documented concern. It is not classified as a carcinogen by the major agencies at cosmetic use levels.
ingredients.irritation: Can dry and irritate skin, scalp and eyes.
ingredients.allergy: True allergy is rare. Most reactions are irritation.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and contact time. Rinse-off use carries less risk than leave-on use.
ingredients.precautions: Rinse thoroughly. Avoid eye contact. Choose milder cleansers if your skin is dry or sensitive.
groups: People with dry, sensitive or eczema-prone skin

ingredients.name: Cocamidopropyl Betaine
ingredients.function: Mild surfactant that boosts foam and softens harsher cleansers.
ingredients.why: Usually well tolerated, but it is a recognised cause of contact allergy in a small number of people. Reactions have often been traced to impurities from manufacturing rather than the molecule itself.
ingredients.health: No notable systemic concern at normal rinse-off use.
ingredients.allergy: Contact allergy is documented in a small number of people.
ingredients.dependsOn: Purity of the raw material and how long it stays on the skin.
ingredients.precautions: Stop use if you develop an itchy rash on the scalp, face or hands.
groups: People who have had contact dermatitis from shampoos or soaps

ingredients.name: Fragrance (Parfum)
ingredients.function: Gives the product a scent.
ingredients.why: One word on a label can stand for many fragrance chemicals, and fragrance is among the most common causes of contact allergy to cosmetics.
ingredients.health: The main documented concern is skin allergy and irritation.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate skin or eyes in some people.
ingredients.allergy: A common cause of contact allergy. The exact chemicals are often not listed.
ingredients.dependsOn: The individual fragrance chemicals, how much is used, and whether the product stays on skin.
ingredients.precautions: Patch test new products on a small area. Choose fragrance-free products if you know you react.
groups: People with a known fragrance allergy
ingredients.regulation: EU rules require recognised fragrance allergens to be listed individually above set thresholds (0.001 percent in leave-on and 0.01 percent in rinse-off products). Indian labelling rules for fragrance components were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Methylisothiazolinone
ingredients.function: Preservative that stops bacteria and mould growing in the product.
ingredients.why: A well-documented cause of allergic contact dermatitis. Rising allergy rates in Europe led regulators to restrict it in cosmetics.
ingredients.health: The main documented concern is skin allergy. Once a person is sensitised the allergy can be long lasting.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and whether the product stays on skin. Leave-on use carries more risk than rinse-off use.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid leave-on products containing it, especially if you have had a skin allergy. Stop use if a rash appears.
groups: People with sensitive skin or past contact dermatitis
ingredients.regulation: In the EU it is not allowed in leave-on cosmetics and is limited to a very low level (0.0015 percent) in rinse-off cosmetics. Its status under Indian cosmetic rules was not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Methylparaben
ingredients.function: Preservative.
ingredients.why: The short-chain parabens have the longest safety record. EU scientific advisers considered methylparaben safe at permitted levels.
ingredients.health: Shows very weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests, far weaker than natural hormones. Regulators judge the permitted levels safe for adults.
ingredients.allergy: Contact allergy is uncommon and tends to occur on damaged skin.
ingredients.dependsOn: Total paraben amount in the product.
ingredients.precautions: None specific for healthy skin. Stop use if you notice a rash.
ingredients.regulation: EU limit: 0.4 percent for a single paraben ester, 0.8 percent for mixtures. Indian limits were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Propylparaben
ingredients.function: Preservative.
ingredients.why: Permitted, but under tighter limits than methylparaben because of open questions about hormone-like activity, especially in young children.
ingredients.health: Weak hormone-like activity in laboratory studies. Regulators set lower limits as a precaution.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and who uses the product. Products for young children are treated more strictly.
ingredients.precautions: Prefer products without these parabens for babies and young children.
ingredients.regulation: In the EU, propylparaben and butylparaben are limited to 0.14 percent combined and are banned in leave-on products meant for the nappy area of children under three. Indian rules were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Phenoxyethanol
ingredients.function: Preservative.
ingredients.why: Widely used and reviewed by EU scientific advisers, who considered it safe at or below the permitted 1 percent level.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at permitted levels. Higher exposure for infants is treated with extra caution by some regulators.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate skin or eyes at higher concentrations.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and the age of the user.
ingredients.precautions: Take extra care with products used on babies. Avoid eye contact.
ingredients.regulation: EU maximum is 1 percent in cosmetic products. Indian limits were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Triclosan
ingredients.function: Antibacterial agent.
ingredients.why: Regulators have questioned its benefit and safety. For hand and body washes the US FDA concluded manufacturers had not shown it was safe and effective, and removed it from that product type.
ingredients.health: Laboratory studies raise questions about hormone effects and antibiotic resistance. Evidence in humans at consumer-use levels is less clear.
ingredients.dependsOn: Product type and concentration. Regulators treat toothpaste, soaps and other products differently.
ingredients.precautions: Plain soap and water is effective for hand washing. Check current rules for the product type you use.
groups: Pregnant people and young children (as a precaution)
ingredients.regulation: In the US, consumer antiseptic washes containing triclosan were removed from the market in 2016. The EU has restricted its uses. Indian status was not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Benzalkonium Chloride
ingredients.function: Disinfectant and preservative.
ingredients.why: Effective against germs, but it can irritate skin, eyes and airways, and it is a known cause of contact allergy.
ingredients.health: Irritation and allergy are the documented concerns. Breathing sprays of cleaning products containing it has been linked to asthma symptoms in workers.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate skin, eyes and airways.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, spray versus liquid use, and ventilation.
ingredients.precautions: Ventilate the room, avoid eye contact, and keep away from children.

ingredients.name: Ethanol (Alcohol Denat.)
ingredients.function: Solvent and antimicrobial. It is the active germ killer in many hand sanitisers.
ingredients.why: Effective as a sanitiser, but it is flammable and can dry or sting skin. Swallowing it is dangerous, especially for children.
ingredients.health: Concerns are fire risk, drying of skin and accidental swallowing.
ingredients.irritation: Can dry skin and sting broken skin or eyes.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, frequency of use and storage.
ingredients.precautions: Keep away from flames and heat. Keep out of reach of children. Do not swallow.

ingredients.name: Isopropyl Alcohol
ingredients.function: Solvent and disinfectant.
ingredients.why: Flammable, drying to skin, and harmful if swallowed. Vapours can irritate the eyes and airways in poorly ventilated rooms.
ingredients.health: Concerns are fire risk, irritation and toxicity if swallowed.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate skin, eyes and airways.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, ventilation and amount used.
ingredients.precautions: Use in a ventilated room, away from flames. Keep out of reach of children.

ingredients.name: Sodium Hypochlorite (Bleach)
ingredients.function: Disinfectant and stain remover.
ingredients.why: A strong, effective disinfectant. Safe use depends on dilution and handling: it irritates or burns skin and eyes when concentrated and gives off harmful gases when mixed with some other cleaners.
ingredients.health: Concentrated product can burn skin and eyes. Fumes can irritate the airways.
ingredients.irritation: Strong irritant to skin, eyes and airways.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, dilution, ventilation and what it is mixed with.
ingredients.precautions: Never mix with acids (such as toilet cleaners or vinegar) or with ammonia. Use gloves and ventilation. Keep away from children.
ingredients.regulation: Hazard labelling depends on concentration. Check the product label.

ingredients.name: Sodium Hydroxide (Caustic Soda)
ingredients.function: Strong alkali used in drain cleaners, and to adjust pH or make soap.
ingredients.why: In concentrated form it is corrosive and causes serious burns to skin and eyes. In finished soaps and cosmetics it is used up or neutralised during manufacture, so little remains.
ingredients.health: Chemical burns on skin and eyes. Swallowing causes serious internal injury.
ingredients.irritation: Corrosive to skin and eyes at high concentration.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration. Drain cleaners are far stronger than the traces in finished soap.
ingredients.precautions: Wear gloves and eye protection with strong cleaners. Never mix with other cleaners. Keep locked away from children. Seek medical help after any splash in the eyes.
ingredients.regulation: Classified as corrosive in hazard labelling when concentrated.

ingredients.name: Ammonia
ingredients.function: Glass and surface cleaner.
ingredients.why: Vapours irritate the eyes, nose and throat, and mixing with bleach releases toxic gas.
ingredients.health: Irritation of eyes and airways. Concentrated product can burn.
ingredients.allergy: Allergy is not the main concern.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, ventilation and what it is mixed with.
ingredients.precautions: Never mix with bleach. Ventilate well. Keep away from children.

ingredients.name: Citric Acid
ingredients.function: Adjusts acidity (pH), adds sourness in food, and removes limescale in cleaners.
ingredients.why: Occurs naturally in citrus fruit and is widely used. Food-safety committees have not set a numerical limit for it in food.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at food or cosmetic levels.
ingredients.irritation: Strong cleaners can irritate eyes and skin. Cosmetic levels are low.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration. Descaling products are stronger than food use.
ingredients.precautions: Wear gloves with strong descaling products.

ingredients.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
ingredients.function: Antioxidant that protects food and skin products. In skincare it is also used for brightening.
ingredients.why: An essential nutrient with a long history of safe use. Food-safety committees have not set a numerical limit for it as an additive.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at food or cosmetic levels.
ingredients.irritation: Strong, acidic skincare serums can sting.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and product pH in skincare.
ingredients.precautions: Patch test strong vitamin C serums.

ingredients.name: Sodium Benzoate
ingredients.function: Preservative.
ingredients.why: Expert committees have set an acceptable daily intake for benzoic acid and its salts and typical intakes are below it.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at permitted levels. In acidic drinks that also contain vitamin C, traces of benzene can form, so manufacturers manage formulation.
ingredients.irritation: May irritate skin at higher concentrations.
ingredients.allergy: Can trigger hives or breathing symptoms in a small number of sensitive people.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount consumed over the day and the other ingredients in the drink.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid if you have noticed reactions to benzoates.
ingredients.regulation: Use levels in food are set by regulators. Check current FSSAI limits for the food type.

ingredients.name: Potassium Sorbate
ingredients.function: Preservative.
ingredients.why: Reviewed by European food-safety scientists, who set an acceptable daily intake for sorbic acid and its salts.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at permitted levels.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount consumed or used.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.
ingredients.regulation: Use levels in food are set by regulators. Check current FSSAI limits for the food type.

ingredients.name: Tartrazine (Yellow Colour)
ingredients.function: Synthetic yellow colour.
ingredients.why: Reported to cause hives or intolerance in a small number of people. After a 2007 study, EU rules require a warning on foods with certain colours, including this one, about possible effects on activity and attention in some children.
ingredients.health: Documented concerns are intolerance reactions and a possible effect on activity and attention in some children.
ingredients.irritation: Not a skin irritant at cosmetic use.
ingredients.allergy: Intolerance and hive-type reactions are reported in a small number of people.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount eaten and individual sensitivity.
ingredients.precautions: Parents of children who react to food colours may choose to avoid it.
groups: People with documented azo dye sensitivity
ingredients.regulation: EU food labelling requires a warning for this colour. Whether it is permitted for a given food in India depends on FSSAI rules, which were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
ingredients.function: Synthetic orange-yellow colour.
ingredients.why: Similar concerns to tartrazine: intolerance reactions in a small number of people and a possible effect on activity and attention in some children, which led to an EU warning label.
ingredients.health: Documented concerns are intolerance reactions and a possible effect on activity and attention in some children.
ingredients.irritation: Not a skin irritant at cosmetic use.
ingredients.allergy: Intolerance and hive-type reactions are reported in a small number of people.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount eaten and individual sensitivity.
ingredients.precautions: Parents of children who react to food colours may choose to avoid it.
ingredients.regulation: EU food labelling requires a warning for this colour. Indian permissions depend on FSSAI rules, which were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Aspartame
ingredients.function: Artificial sweetener.
ingredients.why: Regulators and expert committees consider it safe within the acceptable daily intake, which was reaffirmed in 2023. The same year IARC classified it as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) based on limited evidence. People with phenylketonuria must avoid it.
ingredients.health: Must be avoided by people with phenylketonuria. Other concerns are debated and the evidence is limited.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount consumed relative to body weight.
ingredients.precautions: People with phenylketonuria should avoid it. Others can stay within the acceptable daily intake.
ingredients.regulation: Products containing it must carry a phenylalanine warning in many jurisdictions. Check the current FSSAI labelling text.

ingredients.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
ingredients.function: Flavour enhancer.
ingredients.why: Expert committees have not set a numerical limit for it. Controlled studies have not shown consistent reactions at normal intakes, though some people report short-lived symptoms after large doses.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal food intakes.
ingredients.allergy: Some people report short-lived symptoms such as headache or flushing after large amounts.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount eaten and individual sensitivity.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid if you have noticed reactions.
groups: People who report reactions to MSG
ingredients.regulation: Indian food labelling rules require added MSG to be declared and advise against it in foods for infants under 12 months. Check the current regulation text.

ingredients.name: Sodium Nitrite
ingredients.function: Preservative and colour fixer in cured meats. It also prevents botulism.
ingredients.why: It has a real safety job, but IARC classifies ingested nitrate or nitrite under conditions that favour nitrosamine formation as probably carcinogenic (Group 2A). Regulators limit the amounts allowed.
ingredients.health: Concern is formation of nitrosamines, especially with frequent high intake of cured meats.
ingredients.dependsOn: How often cured meat is eaten and how it is cooked.
ingredients.precautions: Eat cured and processed meats in moderation.
groups: Infants (very young babies are more sensitive to nitrite)
ingredients.regulation: Limits are set by food regulators. Check current FSSAI limits.

ingredients.name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA)
ingredients.function: Antioxidant that stops fats going rancid.
ingredients.why: IARC classifies it as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B) based on animal studies, while food-safety bodies have set an acceptable daily intake that normal diets stay below.
ingredients.health: Concern comes mainly from animal studies at high doses.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount consumed relative to body weight.
ingredients.precautions: Limit very frequent intake of heavily processed fatty snacks.
ingredients.regulation: Limits are set by food regulators. Check current FSSAI limits.

ingredients.name: Sugars
ingredients.function: Sweetener and bulking agent.
ingredients.why: Sugar is not toxic. The concern depends on the amount: the WHO advises keeping free sugars below 10 percent of daily energy, with extra benefit below 5 percent.
ingredients.health: High intake is linked with tooth decay, weight gain and higher risk of type 2 diabetes.
ingredients.dependsOn: Total amount eaten across the day.
ingredients.precautions: Check the nutrition panel for sugar per serving.

ingredients.name: Salt (Sodium Chloride)
ingredients.function: Flavour and preservative in food. Thickener or mild abrasive in cosmetics and cleaners.
ingredients.why: In cosmetics and cleaners it has low concern. In food the concern depends on amount: the WHO advises adults to eat less than 5 grams of salt (2 grams of sodium) per day.
ingredients.health: High salt intake raises blood pressure over time.
ingredients.irritation: High levels can sting broken skin or eyes.
ingredients.dependsOn: Total amount eaten across the day.
ingredients.precautions: Check sodium per serving on food labels.
groups: People with high blood pressure or kidney disease

ingredients.name: Sodium Bicarbonate (Baking Soda)
ingredients.function: Raising agent in food, pH adjuster, mild abrasive and deodoriser.
ingredients.why: Widely used and low in hazard. Food-safety committees have not set a numerical limit for it.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal use.
ingredients.irritation: Can dry or irritate skin with frequent scrubbing.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount. Very large swallowed amounts upset the stomach and body salt balance.
ingredients.precautions: Do not swallow large spoonfuls as a remedy without medical advice.

ingredients.name: Acetic Acid (Vinegar)
ingredients.function: Sour flavour and preservative in food. Descaler and cleaner at home.
ingredients.why: Household vinegar is a dilute solution and low in hazard in food. Stronger cleaning products can irritate eyes and skin, and it must never be mixed with bleach.
ingredients.health: No notable concern in food. Concentrated acetic acid can burn.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate eyes and skin at higher concentrations.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration.
ingredients.precautions: Never mix with bleach. Wear gloves with strong cleaners.

ingredients.name: Xanthan Gum
ingredients.function: Thickener and stabiliser.
ingredients.why: Widely used. Food-safety committees have not set a numerical limit for it, and it is not absorbed by the body.
ingredients.health: Large amounts may cause gas or loose stools.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount eaten.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Titanium Dioxide
ingredients.function: White pigment, opacifier and sunscreen filter.
ingredients.why: Used for decades, but EU food-safety scientists could not rule out a genotoxicity concern for it as a food additive, and the EU stopped authorising it in food in 2022. In cosmetics the concern is mainly breathing in powder or spray forms.
ingredients.health: Concerns are about swallowed particles in food and inhaled powder or spray. Normal skin use is not the main concern.
ingredients.dependsOn: Form (powder or spray versus cream), particle size and route of exposure.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid breathing in loose powder or spray versions.
groups: People who use loose powders or sprays often
ingredients.regulation: Not authorised as a food additive in the EU since 2022. Its status under Indian food and cosmetic rules was not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Talc
ingredients.function: Absorbs moisture and gives a smooth feel in powders and make-up.
ingredients.why: IARC has classified talc as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A), mainly from occupational inhalation, and talc contaminated with asbestos-like fibres as carcinogenic (Group 1). Cosmetic talc is supposed to be free of asbestos.
ingredients.health: Concerns are inhalation of loose powder and possible contamination of poor-quality talc.
ingredients.dependsOn: Whether the powder is breathed in, the purity of the talc and how often it is used.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid breathing in loose powder. Keep it away from babies' faces.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3)
ingredients.function: Skin conditioning ingredient used for oil balance and uneven tone.
ingredients.why: Well tolerated in most people in studies at the concentrations normally used in skincare.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal use.
ingredients.irritation: Higher concentrations can cause flushing or stinging in some people.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration.
ingredients.precautions: Patch test if your skin is sensitive.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid / Sodium Hyaluronate
ingredients.function: Humectant that holds water on the skin surface.
ingredients.why: A large molecule that stays on the skin surface and is well tolerated in safety reviews.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal use.
ingredients.dependsOn: Formulation of the whole product.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.function: Exfoliant used for acne and flaky skin. Also used as a preservative.
ingredients.why: Effective, but can dry and irritate skin, and regulators limit the amounts and uses. Doctors usually advise asking before using strong or large-area products in pregnancy.
ingredients.health: Irritation is the main concern. It is related to aspirin, so large-area use on very young children is avoided.
ingredients.irritation: Can cause dryness, redness and peeling.
ingredients.allergy: People allergic to aspirin should ask a doctor first.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, size of skin area treated and frequency of use.
ingredients.precautions: Start slowly. Use sunscreen. Ask a doctor before use in pregnancy or on young children.
ingredients.regulation: The EU sets maximum concentrations by product type. Indian limits were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Retinol and Related Vitamin A Forms
ingredients.function: Anti-ageing and acne ingredient.
ingredients.why: Effective, but commonly causes redness, dryness and peeling, and makes skin more sensitive to sun. High oral vitamin A is linked to birth defects, so doctors often advise avoiding these products in pregnancy as a precaution.
ingredients.health: Irritation and sun sensitivity are documented. Pregnancy advice is precautionary.
ingredients.irritation: Common at the start of use.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, frequency and sun exposure.
ingredients.precautions: Use at night, wear sunscreen, and ask a doctor before use in pregnancy or while trying to conceive.
ingredients.regulation: The EU has set maximum concentrations by product type. Indian limits were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Alpha Hydroxy Acids (Glycolic and Lactic Acid)
ingredients.function: Exfoliants that loosen dead skin cells.
ingredients.why: The US FDA states that alpha hydroxy acids can increase sensitivity to the sun. Higher concentrations can irritate.
ingredients.health: Main documented concern is increased sun sensitivity and irritation.
ingredients.irritation: Stinging, redness and peeling are possible.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, product pH and sun exposure.
ingredients.precautions: Wear sunscreen and avoid strong peels unless supervised.

ingredients.name: Oxybenzone (Benzophenone-3)
ingredients.function: Chemical UV filter in sunscreens.
ingredients.why: Can cause photo-allergy in some people. It is absorbed through skin, and FDA studies found it in blood after sunscreen use, which the agency says does not by itself mean it is unsafe. It is also restricted in some places over coral reef concerns.
ingredients.health: Photo-allergy is documented. Questions about absorption continue to be studied.
ingredients.allergy: Contact and photo-contact allergy are documented.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, area covered, and sun exposure.
ingredients.precautions: Sunscreen is still important. If you react to it, check labels for other UV filters.
ingredients.regulation: Hawaii prohibits the sale of sunscreens containing oxybenzone and octinoxate from 2021. Indian rules were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Zinc Oxide
ingredients.function: Mineral UV filter, skin protectant and pigment.
ingredients.why: Little is absorbed through healthy skin and it is widely used in sunscreens and nappy creams.
ingredients.health: No notable concern on skin. Inhaling powder or spray forms is the concern.
ingredients.dependsOn: Form: cream versus loose powder or spray.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid breathing in powder or spray versions.

ingredients.name: Petrolatum and Mineral Oil
ingredients.function: Seals in moisture and protects skin.
ingredients.why: Cosmetic-grade versions are highly refined. Safety concerns apply to untreated or mildly treated mineral oils, which IARC classifies as carcinogenic, not to the highly refined grades.
ingredients.health: No notable concern for refined cosmetic grades.
ingredients.irritation: Rarely irritating. Can feel heavy on oily skin.
ingredients.dependsOn: How well the raw material was refined.
ingredients.precautions: Choose products from brands that state the grade is cosmetic or pharmaceutical.

ingredients.name: Dimethicone
ingredients.function: Silicone that makes products feel smooth and protects the skin surface.
ingredients.why: A large molecule that stays on the skin surface and is considered low concern in safety reviews.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal use.
ingredients.dependsOn: Whole formulation.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Cyclopentasiloxane (D5)
ingredients.function: Volatile silicone that gives a light, silky feel.
ingredients.why: Low concern for skin, but the EU restricted D4 and D5 in wash-off products because they persist in the environment.
ingredients.health: No notable skin concern. The main concern is the environment.
ingredients.dependsOn: Whether the product is washed down the drain.
ingredients.precautions: None for personal safety. Environmental concern applies mainly to rinse-off products.
ingredients.regulation: In the EU, D4 and D5 are limited to 0.1 percent in wash-off cosmetics. Indian rules were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Fluoride (Sodium Fluoride and Related)
ingredients.function: Protects teeth against decay in toothpaste and mouthwash.
ingredients.why: Fluoride toothpaste has strong evidence of preventing tooth decay. The concern is young children swallowing it, which can cause white marks on developing teeth (dental fluorosis).
ingredients.health: Benefit for teeth is well established. Concern is over-swallowing in early childhood.
ingredients.dependsOn: Amount of paste used, age and how much is swallowed.
ingredients.precautions: Use a small smear or pea-sized amount for young children and supervise brushing. Follow your dentist's advice.

ingredients.name: Disodium EDTA
ingredients.function: Binds metal ions so products stay stable and do not spoil.
ingredients.why: Low concern for human health at use levels. It breaks down slowly in the environment, which is discussed in environmental assessments.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at use levels.
ingredients.irritation: Can irritate eyes in concentrated form.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Cetyl, Cetearyl and Stearyl Alcohol
ingredients.function: Thickener and softener for creams and conditioners.
ingredients.why: Fatty alcohols are waxy and not drying like ethanol. They are widely used and considered low concern in safety reviews.
ingredients.health: No notable concern.
ingredients.allergy: Contact allergy is rare but reported.
ingredients.dependsOn: Whole formulation.
ingredients.precautions: None specific.

ingredients.name: Tocopherol (Vitamin E)
ingredients.function: Antioxidant.
ingredients.why: A natural nutrient and widely used antioxidant with a long history of safe use.
ingredients.health: No notable concern at normal use.
ingredients.allergy: Contact allergy is rare but reported.

ingredients.name: Linalool
ingredients.function: Fragrance ingredient found in many plants.
ingredients.why: A recognised fragrance allergen. It can oxidise on contact with air, and the oxidised forms are more likely to cause allergy.
ingredients.health: The documented concern is skin allergy.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, product age and storage.
ingredients.precautions: Patch test. Choose fragrance-free products if you react.
ingredients.regulation: EU rules require it to be listed on the label above set thresholds. Indian labelling rules were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: Limonene
ingredients.function: Citrus fragrance and solvent.
ingredients.why: A recognised fragrance allergen, mainly after it oxidises with air exposure.
ingredients.health: The documented concern is skin allergy.
ingredients.allergy: A recognised contact allergen once oxidised.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration, product age and storage.
ingredients.precautions: Patch test. Choose fragrance-free products if you react.
ingredients.regulation: EU rules require it to be listed on the label above set thresholds. Indian labelling rules were not verified in this dataset.

ingredients.name: DMDM Hydantoin
ingredients.function: Preservative that slowly releases small amounts of formaldehyde.
ingredients.why: Formaldehyde causes contact allergy in some people and is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly after breathing it in at high levels. Releasers are used at low levels but can still trigger allergy.
ingredients.health: Contact allergy is the main documented concern at cosmetic use levels.
ingredients.dependsOn: Concentration and how much formaldehyde is released.
ingredients.precautions: Avoid if you are allergic to formaldehyde. Stop use if a rash appears.
ingredients.regulation: In the EU, products releasing enough formaldehyde (above 0.05 percent in the finished product) must carry a warning. Indian rules were not verified in this dataset.
